asDecan.p: Your Sun falls between ten and nineteen degrees of Aquarius, the middle third, where the sign is settled and at full strength. The Golden Dawn gives each ten-degree slice of a sign, a decan, its own planet, and this one goes to Mercury, the planet of thinking, talking and getting from place to place. Mercury has no special dignity in Aquarius, which means it's a visitor there, neither helped nor held back. Aquarius is ruled by Saturn in the old system and Uranus in the modern one, so Mercury here picks up Saturn's patience and Uranus's knack for looking at things from somewhere odd. The Five of Swords before you is Venus's, and it's about who won the argument. The Seven after you is the Moon's, and it slips off quietly with what it wants. Yours is the one where somebody goes somewhere, a ferryman poling his passengers over to flat water. The Star is your Sun card, and this is the ten degrees inside it where you sit.

You think better on the move, and you've probably known that since you were a kid. On a Sunday with nothing planned you'll often end up on a long drive, or on a train to somewhere you don't need to go, just to sort your head out. There's a saved search somewhere, or a folder, of places you might live one day, and you look at it more than you'd admit. Friends text you before they book anything, because you'll know which airport's cheaper and how long the transfer really takes. At a family dinner you're usually explaining the older relatives' phones to them and the younger ones' slang back the other way. And in a meeting that's turned into two people shouting, you pick up a pen and ask, fairly mildly, what they actually agree on.

You're good at getting other people out of things. When a friend finally decides to leave a bad marriage or a job that's grinding her down, you're the one who turns up with boxes, finds the rental listings and knows what to say to the landlord. You don't make anyone talk about their feelings before they're ready. You get them moving, and the talking happens halfway through the packing, which is often when people can actually manage it. I've seen this a lot with Suns in this part of Aquarius. They end up as the person in the family who gets the late call, a sister ringing at eleven at night to say she's in the car and doesn't know where to go. You're calm on those calls in a way that settles the other person, and by the end of it she usually knows where she's sleeping.

The one people miss is how fast you reach for the exit, for other people as well as yourself. A friend grumbles about her job for ten minutes and you've already sent her three job ads. Your brother has one bad month with his girlfriend and you're asking whether he's thought about leaving. Sometimes that's exactly what someone needs to hear. Often they wanted to complain and then go back and fix it, and they come away feeling their life was being tidied for them. The other habit is carrying messages. In a family feud you end up passing things along, what Mum said, what your sister meant by it, and because Mercury is good with words you soften both sides. It keeps the peace for a while. It also means those two never have to speak to each other, and when it blows up, the go-between takes the blame.

When something goes badly wrong, a death in the family or a job falling through, you go straight to the logistics, and you do them for everybody. You ring the relatives, sort the paperwork, drive your aunt to the airport, and you're genuinely useful to everyone in the room. A week later you've usually moved in some way. You've booked a trip, rearranged the whole flat, or started looking at jobs in another city, and you'll say you're fine and mean it. The feeling tends to catch up months on, somewhere quiet, a hotel room or a long drive home. The cost is that people can't find you. Your partner wants to grieve alongside you and you're already busy with the next thing. What helps is staying put for a bit. Keep the same routine, see the same two friends, and let somebody sit with you before you plan anything.

A lot of people with this Sun meet their partners in transit. On a trip, in the first month of a job in a new city, halfway through a move. Aquarius's opposite sign is Leo, and you often end up with someone warmer and more openly affectionate, someone who wants to hear that they're loved in so many words. You show it by sorting things out. You find the cheaper flights, fill in the form they've been dreading, send the name of a good physio for their dad's knee, and in your head that's obviously love. Often your partner is still waiting for you to say it. You need someone who doesn't take your need for distance personally. A long walk after a row, before you can talk, is how you come back, and a partner who follows you out the door usually makes it worse.

Mercury deals in messages and movement, and in Aquarius it takes to systems, so you're good at work that gets people or information from one state to another. Relocation, logistics, IT migrations, change management, helping staff through a redundancy, teaching adults who are retraining. You're often the one brought in when a team's in a mess, and you get them through it without much drama. The catch comes once things are calm. You like the part where everything's changing and you get restless when it's done, so you can end up switching jobs every three years without ever quite choosing to. That's fine if you know it about yourself. It's worth looking for work where the change is the job itself, like consulting, project teams or anything with regular travel.

At twenty, people with this Sun often seem a bit cooler than their friends. They're the steady ones during everyone else's break-ups, and their own lives are kept tidy and fairly private. There's usually at least one big move early, leaving home young, changing countries, dropping one course to start another. By the mid-thirties the moving tends to catch up with them. Something they left without really feeling comes back, a parent they moved away from, an old relationship, a town, and it has to be sat through the slow way, which Mercury doesn't enjoy. That's often when this decan gets warmer, and a lot easier to be close to. The fifties tend to bring a settledness nobody saw coming, least of all them. A house they stay in, friends of thirty years, and a real knack for helping younger people through their own big changes.

The next time something rattles you and you feel the pull to go, the booking site open, the real estate app, the car keys in your hand, give it forty-eight hours first. Stay where you are, keep your ordinary routine, and don't book, apply for or sign anything. Write down on paper what you were hoping the move would fix. If you still want to go after two days, go, and take the list with you.
